name: Rayleigh-Benard Convection — Lorenz Three-Mode Model
description: Source reconstruction of Lorenz (1963), equations (25)-(27), pp.134-136: the signed convection X, horizontal temperature Y and vertical thermal-profile Z amplitudes form a nonlinear three-mode free-boundary Rayleigh-Benard truncation. The original generated ramp-heated two-temperature exponential model was not executable Rayleigh physics and is replaced by these published equations, parameters sigma10, r28, a-squared0.5 and initial (0,1,0) from Table1. Time is dimensionless tau, not seconds. The saved horizon0..200 is retained; the integration grid is refined from0.1 to the paper's0.01 dimensionless time step, with RK4. The paper used a double-approximation method, not RK4. The removed physical parameters and heating/cooling laws are archived in the repair receipt; they cannot consistently describe these dimensionless modes. This low-order educational model is not a calibrated fluid simulation; Lorenz explicitly warns that strongly convecting PDE solutions need not resemble its extreme truncation. Negative X/Y mean reversed circulation, not negative absolute temperature.
reference: Lorenz EN (1963). Deterministic Nonperiodic Flow. J Atmos Sci20:130-141. Equations21-27 and Table1, pp.134-136. Primary paper scan inspected 2026-10-20: https://samizdat.co/works/do-while/lorenz-1963.pdf
